solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Town planner ultimately avoids putting in effort

indicators.note: the effort word steers clear of the letter, so that letter is dropped from it

parts.note: someone putting in effort is working

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of planner

explanation.surface: A town planner is accused of shirking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives R, the last letter of 'planner', and 'avoids' takes that R out of WORKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Woking is a commuter town in Surrey, south-west of London.

clue.text: Take after Old Boney?

indicators.note: after places the take word behind the old letter

parts.note: to steal is to take

explanation.surface: Someone resembles an old man known as Boney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take after' reads as resemble, and 'Old Boney' as Napoleon's nickname; it means bony, to do with the skeleton.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is a medical adjective meaning relating to bone.

clue.text: Original third of Three Wise Men meeting Son

parts.note: one is a third of three, written as I
the Magi were the three wise men of the nativity story
a native is a son of a place, as in a son of the soil

explanation.surface: One of the three kings arrives with a boy, as in a nativity play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third of Three' wants a letter of 'Three'; it is one, I, a third of three.
explanation.definitionFit: An original person or work shows fresh ideas, creative and inventive.

clue.text: Throw away photograph

definitions.meaning: to discard or be rid of something
to take a picture of, read as obtain a snap of

explanation.definitionFit: Get rid of something, or literally obtain a camera snap of it.

clue.text: Parrot barely even swinging both ways, carried by master

indicators.note: the master word holds the other pieces within it, as if carrying them

parts.note: a lord is a master

indicators.note: barely here means stripped bare, the word losing its outside letters

parts.note: slang for bisexual, shortened to BI

explanation.surface: A parrot balanced on a swinging perch is held by its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swinging both ways' is slang for bisexual, BI; 'barely' strips the outer letters of 'even', and 'carried by' sets the pieces inside the master word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovebirds are small African birds of the parrot family.

clue.text: Support large City trader, striking radical note

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London

indicators.note: striking means crossing out, so those letters are struck from trader

parts.note: N is a note in crossword shorthand

explanation.surface: A large City trader takes a radical stance by going on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' removes RAD from TRADER, leaving TER. The City is London's financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a stand that props up a book or notes for a reader.

clue.text: Begrudging losing space in the contest

indicators.note: losing means the space word is dropped from the start

parts.note: envying is begrudging
an en is a printer's space

explanation.surface: A jealous competitor loses ground in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printing space; 'losing' takes EN off ENVYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Those vying are competing, so taking part in a contest.

clue.text: Time to leave spa? Nonsense!

indicators.note: the time letter leaves, departing from the spa word

parts.note: Bath is a spa town in Somerset

explanation.surface: A visitor is told it's time to quit the spa, and refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: BATH, the Somerset spa town, loses T for time.
explanation.definitionFit: Bah is an exclamation of contempt, like humbug.

clue.text: Meditative weak individual pressing mother to stay at home

indicators.note: the weak individual squeezes round the rest, pressing it inside

parts.note: the runt is the weakest of a litter

indicators.note: the at home word stays put inside the mother word

parts.note: ma is mother
in means at home

explanation.surface: A weakling forces a mother to stay indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to stay' puts IN in MA (MINA); 'pressing' puts that inside RUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruminant as an adjective means contemplative, chewing over thoughts as a cow chews the cud.

clue.text: Transcontinental body finally replacing Pole in charge

indicators.note: one pole letter takes the place of the other inside the word for finally

parts.note: at last means finally
N is the North Pole, swapped in for S, the South Pole

explanation.surface: A railway company finally gets a new Polish boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacing' swaps the S of AT LAST for N, the other pole, giving ATLANT. 'Pole' wants to mean a person from Poland; it is a magnetic pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Atlantic Ocean is a body of water lying across between the continents of Europe, Africa and the Americas.

clue.text: Much of train hum eradicated in place underground

indicators.note: only part of the three words is used, a run of letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: A train's annoying hum has mostly been eliminated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much of' takes a run from trAIN HUM Eradicated: the answer sits inside those words.
explanation.definitionFit: To inhume is to bury, putting a body in the ground.

clue.text: Exile turned in during strike

indicators.note: during shows one piece placed in the course of, so inside, the other

parts.note: to bash is to strike

indicators.note: turned means the little word in is read backwards

explanation.surface: A deportation was ordered in the middle of an industrial strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' reads as industrial action in the surface, but is the verb bash; 'turned' reverses 'in' and 'during' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to send them away from their country, to expel them.

clue.text: Perhaps intend filling G&T with fruit

parts.note: EG, for example, signals that something is only a possibility

indicators.note: the intend word goes into the drink like a filling

parts.note: G&T is gin and tonic, giving the letters G and T
to plan is to intend

explanation.surface: Someone means to add some fruit to their gin and tonic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' puts PLAN inside G and T, after EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Aubergine, the purple vegetable, is botanically a berry, the fruit of a plant in the nightshade family.

clue.text: Drink honey up, with Young's regularly put down

indicators.note: up reverses the honey word, as written in a down entry

parts.note: mel is Latin for honey, used in pharmacy

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word

parts.note: to squash is to put down, crush

explanation.surface: A father drinks mead while his son's remarks are routinely dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MEL (Latin for honey) to LEM; 'regularly' takes ON from Young's.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon squash is a British soft-drink concentrate diluted with water.

clue.text: Wonder on opening Times hasn't changed

indicators.note: the little word on opens the answer, placed at its front
changed tells us the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Amazement that the newspaper has stayed the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' puts ON first; 'changed' rearranges TIMES and HASNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Astonishment is great surprise or amazement, a sense of wonder.

clue.text: Twisted artist lines inside of saw

indicators.note: the artist and lines go inside the saw word

parts.note: spied means saw
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
L stands for line, LL for lines

explanation.surface: A painter draws lines inside a saw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' wants to be the tool; it is the past tense of see, SPIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiralled means wound in coils, curled round.

clue.text: Key protecting Picasso, say? Not from him!

definitions.text: Key protecting Picasso, say? Not from him!

indicators.note: the key word guards the art, holding it inside

parts.note: chief means key, main
a Picasso painting is an example of art

explanation.surface: A guard keeps the masterpiece safe from a robber.
explanation.walkthrough: The Citroen Picasso is a car, so you protect it from this criminal; 'Picasso' also gives ART, a work by the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steals vehicles, such as a Citroen Picasso, is the one your car needs guarding from.

clue.text: Problem with Listener certain if one blunders

indicators.note: the words go wrong, their letters falling into a new order

explanation.surface: A listener to the radio worries over a mistake they may have made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blunders' rearranges CERTAIN IF ONE. 'Listener' wants to be a person; it is an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear infection, such as otitis, is a medical trouble affecting the organ of hearing.

clue.text: Standard conflict largely sign of Speaker's error

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a clash is a conflict
sic marks a mistake made by the person quoted

explanation.surface: A dispute arises largely over a Commons Speaker's blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts CLASH to CLAS; SIC is inserted in a quote to show the error was the original speaker's.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work held up as a standard of excellence.

clue.text: Festival briefly fully opened up Area 51

indicators.note: up reverses the shortened word, as read in a down entry
briefly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: wide, as in wide open, means fully opened
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A secretive military base is opened to the public for a short celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts WIDE to WID, and 'up' turns it to DIW. Area 51 is the secret US base, but here it's A + LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights, held in autumn.

clue.text: Time to welcome Conservative hosted by head of France and the rest

indicators.note: the time word takes in the rest, as a host welcomes a guest

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: the Conservative letter is a guest inside the French head

parts.note: tete is the French word for head
C abbreviates Conservative, the British party

explanation.surface: Time for a Tory to be entertained by the French president and everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosted by' puts C in TETE (French for 'head') to make TCETE; 'to welcome' sets that inside ERA. 'head of France' wants to mean F; it is French for head.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera, Latin, is used to mean and so on, the remaining items.

clue.text: Finally become parody after dismissing leader

indicators.note: the parody word loses its first letter, its leader

parts.note: a send-up is a parody

explanation.surface: A spoof ends up firing its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing leader' drops the S from SEND-UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up somewhere is to arrive there eventually, as a final outcome.

clue.text: Causer of climate change almost completely clear

parts.note: AC is air conditioning, which changes the climate of a room

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is cut from the completely word

parts.note: quite can mean completely, as in quite right

explanation.surface: An environmental villain is almost entirely exonerated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Causer of climate change' looks like global warming; it is air conditioning, AC. 'almost' cuts QUITE to QUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit an accused person is to declare them not guilty, freeing them of the charge.

clue.text: Two wrongs make a … sailor?

parts.note: a sin is one wrong
bad is a wrong, the second of the two

explanation.surface: Playing on the saying two wrongs don't make a right.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says two wrongs don't make a right; here two wrongs make the sailor of the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Sindbad, of the Arabian Nights tales, was a legendary mariner.

clue.text: View live television to begin with

parts.note: to be is to live, exist

indicators.note: to begin with takes just the opening letter of television

explanation.surface: Someone sits down to watch live TV.
explanation.walkthrough: BE (live) plus T, the first letter of 'television'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bet can mean an opinion, as in my bet is it will rain.

clue.text: Save a tennis organisation through influence

indicators.note: the influence word runs right through the others, enclosing them

parts.note: sway means influence
LTA is the Lawn Tennis Association, governing body of British tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis body gets funds through lobbying.
explanation.walkthrough: The LTA, the Lawn Tennis Association, runs British tennis; 'through' sets A and it inside the influence word.
explanation.definitionFit: To salt away money is to store it up for the future, putting it by.

clue.text: Government department almost admitting Crown's irrelevant

indicators.note: the department word lets the crown word in, taking it inside
almost means the last letter of the department word is dropped

parts.note: an office is a government department, like the Home Office
the crown of the head is the top

explanation.surface: A ministry concedes that the monarchy no longer matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crown' reads as the monarchy, but it is the top of the head; 'almost' trims the department word before 'admitting' takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark that is off-topic strays from the subject under discussion.

clue.text: International line took over a Mexican plant

indicators.note: over turns the preceding pieces backwards, as in a down entry

parts.note: had means took, as in had lunch

explanation.surface: An international railway company buys out a Mexican business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses I + L + HAD to give DAHLI; A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The dahlia is a garden flower native to Mexico, its national flower.
